title: AIcrowd | Studio 1947
description: One picture per problem: how we turn AIcrowd's AI research challenges into visuals anyone can understand, for competitions run with Sony, AWS, AGI House and Meta.

sections.heading: Sounding Video Generation (SVG) Challenge 2024
sections.label: For Sony
body: Video and sound that actually match up, not just play side by side.

media.alt: Sounding Video Generation Challenge banner set: the wide banner and the square link-preview banner side by side, Sony and AIcrowd marks, the challenge title, an audio waveform blending into a glowing play button, $35,000 USD cash prize

body: Sony asked AI teams to build models that create video and sound together, so a bark lands exactly when the dog barks on screen. It's a hard problem, and $35,000 went to the teams who cracked it best.
The visual choice is simple: a soundwave flows straight into a play button, right at the point sound becomes picture. That's the whole idea in one image.

Entries were judged on two things: matching a sound to the exact video frame it belongs to, and placing that sound realistically in space. Most teams built on diffusion models trained to generate video and audio together.
See the challenge on AIcrowd

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The same wave-into-play-button artwork appears everywhere: the site banner, the link preview, even the entry cards. Wherever someone comes across this challenge, it looks and feels the same.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: You understand the challenge before you've read a word. The picture already says it: sound and video, meeting perfectly.

sections.heading: Global Chess Challenge 2025
sections.label: For AWS Trainium & AGI House
body: Can a small AI still play solid chess, and explain its own moves?

media.alt: Global Chess Challenge 2025 banner set: AWS Trainium, AGI House and AIcrowd marks, a chess king on a microchip wafer, Train LLMs to Play Chess, USD 60,000 cash prize, alongside a square link-preview crop of the same artwork

body: AGI House wanted to know if small, lightweight AI models can play real chess, legally and well, and explain their thinking in plain words. Hundreds of teams tried, and $60,000 went to the best of them.

Entries were small AI models, no chess engine or lookup allowed, that had to play a legal move and explain it in one plain sentence. Each was scored on how close its moves came to a top chess engine's, before the best went head to head in a final tournament.

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: We turned the chessboard into a circuit board. Each piece became a glowing node on a microchip, so the board reads as both a game and a machine thinking.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: It says what the challenge is really about at a glance: not just chess, but how a machine reasons.

body: The video's thumbnail uses the same chess-piece-on-a-chip artwork, so it stands out instantly in a crowded feed.
Made at AIcrowd · Concept & design Rabi
See the challenge on AIcrowd

sections.heading: Meta CRAG-MM Challenge 2025
sections.label: For Meta
body: Can an AI answer a question just by looking at a photo, the way a person would?

media.alt: Meta CRAG-MM Challenge 2025 banner: KDD Cup 2025 CRAG-MM Challenge, Improve RAG with Real-World Benchmarks, a pair of smart glasses whose lenses show a chat exchange about a cafe rating and a city skyline with question marks, USD 33000 prize

body: Meta wanted AI that could look at a picture and answer real questions about it correctly, without making things up. Many of the photos were shot from a first-person view, like you're wearing the camera yourself.
So that's exactly what the key visual shows: a pair of glasses, with the conversation happening right inside the lenses. You're not looking at the idea, you're looking through it.
The challenge used thousands of real photos, many shot first-person through smart glasses, and scored answers on getting it right, and on honestly saying "I don't know" rather than guessing.
Made at AIcrowd · Made for Meta · Concept & design Rabi
See the challenge on AIcrowd

cards.title: Art direction
cards.body: The chat and the skyline sit inside the lenses themselves, not beside them. It's a small choice with a big effect: you're seeing the world exactly as the AI does.

cards.title: Why it works
cards.body: One glance and you understand: this is AI that sees what you see.

sections.heading: What this taught the studio
body: Years of working with AIcrowd taught us something simple: even the most technical idea can be told as a picture anyone understands. Every banner we make, whether it's about sound, chess or smart glasses, starts with one question: what's the simplest image that tells this story?

When deep-tech platforms, AI researchers and enterprise data teams look for a creative partner, they don't want a traditional graphic agency. They need someone who is comfortable with abstract maths, clear communication and interactive data visualisation. The task is big: take a complex, many-sided machine learning challenge and frame it so the world's best data scientists can grasp the problem at once, benchmark their models and push science forward.

Our work with AIcrowd is the longest technical design relationship in our company's history. Our CEO, Rabiul Islam, started it years ago, before Studio 1947 formally existed. It has grown into a strong working framework. Together we have shaped the visual identity and communication for world-defining AI challenges hosted with institutions like NeurIPS, Meta, Amazon and the KDD Cup.

_sourceSections.heading: The Core Triad: Science, Communication, Visualisation
body: To connect complex algorithms with human understanding, our workflow rests on three fixed pillars:

_sourceSections.label: Science
body: We get our team deep into the mechanics of each challenge, whether that is reinforcement learning, multi-modal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or clinical biomedical telemetry.

_sourceSections.label: Communication
body: We build clear information hierarchies and narrative frames that remove confusion, so developer communities around the world quickly understand scoring metrics and data parameters.

_sourceSections.label: Visualisation
body: We make high-fidelity key visuals, dynamic leaderboard assets and technical UI that turn dry mathematical formulas into rich, inspiring and useful design.

_sourceSections.heading: Phase 1: The Legacy Era
body: Before Studio 1947 was formally set up, our CEO Rabiul Islam laid the groundwork for this deep-tech design method. He led individual consulting tracks for AIcrowd's most important enterprise benchmarks.

_sourceSections.label: Amazon KDD Cup 2024
body: Benchmarking Large Language Models on how well they handle complex, multi-task digital commerce tasks (for example, personalised shopping tracking, understanding query intent and product recommendations).

We built a visual system that balanced Amazon's corporate identity with a refined network-graph look. The artwork mapped the layered tracks of LLMs parsing data strings. It turned dry e-commerce data into an inviting playground for NLP engineering talent worldwide.

media.alt: Amazon KDD Cup 2024 challenge key visual: network-graph artwork mapping multi-task LLM commerce tracks

_sourceSections.label: ADDI: Alzheimer's Detection Challenge
body: Using advanced data science pipelines to detect and track biomarkers for early-stage Alzheimer's disease in clinical medical trials.

Healthcare data needs absolute precision and real human empathy. We moved right away from cold, sterile tech patterns. Instead we made an organic, data-led composition focused on neural pathway connections and structural brain metrics. The interface put crisp, readable typographic grids first, for medical researchers scanning complex rules.

media.alt: ADDI Alzheimer's Detection Challenge key visual, organic neural pathway composition over a typographic grid

_sourceSections.label: Scene Understanding for Autonomous Drone Delivery (SUADD '23)
body: Computer vision models trained for real-time semantic segmentation, depth estimation and obstacle avoidance in flight routing.

We made machine vision itself the key visual. We laid bright vector tracking grids, bounding boxes and pixel-level depth heatmaps over scenic aerial landscapes. Developers scanning the page could see the exact goal of the computer vision model straight away.

media.alt: SUADD '23 key visual: vector tracking grids, bounding boxes and depth heatmaps over an aerial landscape

_sourceSections.label: Data Purchasing Challenge 2022
body: Simulating automated algorithmic marketplaces where AI agents must evaluate, bid on and buy high-value datasets on a limited budget.

To ground an abstract marketplace, we built a sharp, structured system asset that echoed algorithmic trading floors. Clean geometric arrays and dark-mode data nodes gave the identity the feel of quantitative finance and data as a commodity.

media.alt: Data Purchasing Challenge 2022 key visual: geometric arrays and dark-mode data nodes evoking an algorithmic trading floor

_sourceSections.label: Multi-Agent Behavior Challenge 2022
body: Mapping, predicting and classifying the intricate social and physical paths of interacting multi-agent systems (for example, automated tracking of animal models in neuroscience, or multi-robot swarms).

We designed a complex choreography of motion lines. Using the brand's neon colour gradients, we traced crossing path arrays and emerging behavioural clusters. The key art showed how the science tracks each agent's intent within a busy, unified group.

media.alt: Multi-Agent Behavior Challenge 2022 key visual, intersecting neon motion trajectories forming behavioural clusters

_sourceSections.label: NeurIPS 2021: AWS DeepRacer: AI Driving Olympics Challenge
body: Advanced reinforcement learning models trained to drive scale-model autonomous vehicles around unpredictable, high-speed physical racing tracks.

We merged AWS corporate branding with the high-octane world of motorsport. The design system used sharp velocity lines, technical racing track grids and telemetry dashboard indicators. Together they capture the intense, micro-second optimisation that autonomous driving agents need.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2021 AWS DeepRacer key visual: velocity lines, racing track grids and telemetry indicators

_sourceSections.label: NeurIPS 2020: Procgen Competition
body: Testing how well AI agents' reinforcement learning generalises inside procedurally generated 2D game environments.

We paid homage to classic 8-bit and 16-bit retro developer environments, but lifted the look with clean, modular vector structure. The design showed how endless randomised game levels grow from a fixed set of underlying code rules. It spoke directly to the gaming and ML research crowd.

media.alt: NeurIPS 2020 Procgen Competition key visual: retro 8-bit game environments rebuilt as clean modular vector tiles

_sourceSections.heading: Phase 2: The Studio 1947 Era
body: After Studio 1947 officially launched, our agency took full design ownership of AIcrowd's modern product track. We moved from standalone assets to building complete, layered visual systems for the next generation of machine learning.

_sourceSections.label: Global Chess Challenge 2025
body: Deep-learning neural networks trained to evaluate non-traditional board structures, graph networks and complex predictive game trees.

We completely reimagined the traditional chessboard as a mathematical matrix field. Physical chess pieces became minimal vector nodes projecting calculated paths. The creative direction linked timeless human strategy with the depth of modern AI processing.

media.alt: Global Chess Challenge 2025 key visual: chessboard reimagined as a matrix field with minimalist vector piece nodes

_sourceSections.label: Commonsense Persona-Grounded Dialogue Challenge 2025
body: Pushing conversational NLP engines to keep logical consistency, common-sense reasoning and careful persona tracking across multi-turn dialogues.

Showing human personality through code takes several abstract layers. We built a system of overlapping typographic thought clouds and semantic matching matrices. It shows how an algorithm weighs context, empathy and logic while generating text in conversation with a person.

media.alt: Commonsense Persona-Grounded Dialogue Challenge 2025 key visual, typographic thought clouds over semantic matching matrices

_sourceSections.label: Meta CRAG Multi-Modal Challenge 2025
body: Taking Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) further by asking engineers to fuse real-time web text with complex video, image and speech inputs, under Meta's technical guidelines.

Working within strict institutional rules, we built a premium, dark-mode visual framework for data fusion. It shows separate raw media formats dissolving into a single, high-performance retrieval pipeline. The result is a polished visual presence that matches Meta's engineering standards.

media.alt: Meta CRAG Multi-Modal Challenge 2025 key visual, dark-mode data fusion of video, image and speech into one retrieval pipeline

_sourceSections.label: Sounding Video Generation (SVG) Challenge 2024
body: Generative models that analyse video feeds and produce matching high-fidelity spatial audio, perfectly in sync with the visual timeline.

A masterclass in cross-modal visualisation. We built a striking grid system that blends audio frequency spectrograms with cinematic video strip layouts. The design maps how sound waves rise directly out of motion. It gives generative media researchers a beautiful, harmonious challenge interface.

media.alt: Sounding Video Generation Challenge 2024 key visual, audio frequency spectrograms blended into cinematic video strips

_sourceSections.heading: The Strategic Studio Takeaway
body: Our decade-long work with AIcrowd shows our biggest advantage: we speak deep-tech fluently. We avoid generic, shallow tech templates. Instead, Studio 1947 delivers rigorous, data-faithful visual design that respects the intelligence of the scientific community. Every challenge interface, dataset callout and enterprise brand asset looks authoritative and inspiring, and ready to rally the world's finest algorithmic minds.
